name: Bank Statement Converter
description: Single-feature tool that pulls transactions out of PDF bank statements into clean Excel, used by accountants, bookkeepers and small businesses (founder-stated). Solo founder Angus Cheng, Hong Kong; launched March 2021 (founder-stated). Pricing at the 2023 write-up: $30/mo for 400 pages, $99/mo for 4,000 pages, custom above that (founder-stated, 2023).

mentions.evidence: MRR ~$40,000 (founder-stated); claims ~$39k of that is profit MRR trajectory: $6k (2022) → $14k (2023) → $27k (2024) → $40k (2025) (founder-stated) ~75,000 total users, ~1,000 paying customers, ~40k visits/month (founder-stated) Note: not Stripe-verified. For contrast, TrustMRR-verified clone Bankstatemently (PDF → CSV/XLSX/QBO) shows only $375 MRR / 14 subs / $1.4k all-time, sync stale since 4 Aug 2026.
mentions.indieAngle: Same playbook for a narrower format: Polish bank statements → JPK/KSeF-friendly CSV, or PDF invoices → QuickBooks/Xero import files. Pure conversion, priced by pages.

whyItPrints: Banks still hand out PDFs; accountants still need CSVs. One job, done well, found via organic search. Paid ads never worked for him (~$1k spent for ~$300 in sales, founder-stated).
whyThisMatters:
Single-feature tool that pulls transactions out of PDF bank statements into clean Excel, used by accountants, bookkeepers and small businesses. Solo founder Angus Cheng, Hong Kong; launched March 2021. Pricing at the 2023 write-up: 30 dollars a month for 400 pages, 99 dollars a month for 4,000 pages, custom above that.

Banks still hand out PDFs; accountants still need CSVs. One job, done well, found via organic search. Paid ads never worked for him (1k dollars spent for 300 dollars in sales, founder-stated).

You upload the PDF the bank sent. It returns the rows an accountant can open in a spreadsheet. Angus Cheng builds it in Hong Kong, and it has been up since 2021. The older price list was a monthly plan sized by how many pages you run. He says people find it through search, and that ads did not pay for themselves. The monthly number is his, from a 2025 interview, not a Stripe connection.
